meta.title: MERIT data flow: web request and background job pathways

views.label: Web to Contracts
views.note: Controller checks its permission policy and antiforgery token; JSON binds into a Merit.Contracts record, never a domain type.

views.label: Contracts to Application
views.note: Controller maps the DTO to one service call. The service validates input and calls session.Require(permission) again.

views.label: Application to Domain
views.note: Services pass plain values to pure Domain rules (normalize, population, classify, match) and get decisions back. No I/O crosses.

views.label: Domain to Data
views.note: Application saves the decision through an I*Data port; Data.SqlServer sets SESSION_CONTEXT and runs stored procedures under RLS.

views.label: Worker to Application
views.note: JobWorker claims a queued row (READPAST), reopens the queuing session's profile and tenant, then JobDispatcher runs the job by type.

cards.title: Synchronous pathway (one HTTP request)
items: Merit.Web: authentication, permission policy and antiforgery run before the action; the action binds a Merit.Contracts DTO (API) or a view model (htmx)
Application service validates, checks the permission again, and calls pure Domain rules
The service persists through its I*Data port; the response is mapped back to a Contracts DTO or a partial view

cards.title: Asynchronous pathway (background job)
items: A web action enqueues the job in the same request, for example an intake upload writes the batch and its dbo.jobQueue row
JobWorker polls, claims one row with UPDLOCK + READPAST, and opens a session with the requester's profile, view-as and acting tenant stored on the job
JobDispatcher runs intakeBatch (IntakeProcessor), extractRun (ExtractBuilder) or clusterDetection, then completes or fails the job

cards.title: At each folder boundary
items: Web to Contracts: transport types only; controllers never expose Domain types
Contracts to Application: one service call per action; the service owns validation and permission checks
Application to Domain: values in, decisions out; Domain has no dependencies and no I/O
Domain to Data: drawn for the chain; the Application service makes the call through a port that Data implements

cards.title: Persistence (shared by both pathways)
items: Every connection sets read-only SESSION_CONTEXT (scope key, user, acting tenant)
Only stored procedures run; row-level security filters reads and blocks writes outside the session's tenants and access level
